title: Pushforward of quasi-coherent sections supported on a closed subset
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], where quasi-compact means that inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact. Let $Z\subseteq Y$ be a closed subset such that $Y\setminus Z$ is retrocompact, meaning its intersection with every affine open of $Y$ is quasi-compact. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Define subsheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] by $\mathcal K_X(W)=\{s\in\mathcal F(W):s|_{W\setminus f^{-1}Z}=0\}$ for open $W\subseteq X$ and $\mathcal K_Y(U)=\{t\in(f_*\mathcal F)(U):t|_{U\setminus Z}=0\}$ for open $U\subseteq Y$, where $(f_*\mathcal F)(U)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}U)$ with its induced $\mathcal O_Y(U)$-action. Then $X\setminus f^{-1}Z$ is retrocompact, $\mathcal K_X$, $f_*\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal K_Y$ are quasi-coherent, and $f_*\mathcal K_X=\mathcal K_Y$ as actual submodules of $f_*\mathcal F$. If $\beta:\mathcal H\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves on $Y$, then $\beta$ identifies the subsheaf of sections of $\mathcal H$ zero off $Z$ with $f_*\mathcal K_X$.

source.place: Tag 07ZQ, lemma-push-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, statement and hint (3904--3923); quasi-coherence via Tag 07ZP.

proof.text: Put $V=Y\setminus Z$ and $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$. By the stated definition of retrocompactness, $j^{-1}(U)=V\cap U$ is quasi-compact for every affine open $U\subseteq Y$, so $j$ is quasi-compact. Its base change along $f$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). This base change is the open inclusion $j_X:f^{-1}V\hookrightarrow X$: a map to $X$ factors through this open precisely when its composite to $Y$ factors through $V$, which is the fibre-product universal property. Consequently $W\cap f^{-1}V=j_X^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact for every affine open $W\subseteq X$. Since $f^{-1}V=X\setminus f^{-1}Z$, this proves retrocompactness of the required complement. Continuity of $f$ makes $f^{-1}Z$ closed.

source.place: Tag 07ZQ, lemma-push-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, first sentence of proof hint; Schemes Tag 01K5, lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change

proof.text: Restriction along an open immersion preserves quasi-coherence. For each of the quasi-compact open inclusions j_X and j_Y constructed in Step 1, apply [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] to the restriction of the relevant quasi-coherent module. Its direct image is quasi-coherent because an open immersion is separated. The actual supportedModuleKernel is the kernel of the canonical restriction unit, so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] proves its quasi-coherence. Apply [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] also to f and F for the middle clause. This is exactly the kernel argument in Stacks 07ZP(3), avoiding its additional finite-generation and ideal-power conclusions.

proof.text: The proved source-library theorem range_map_kernelι computes the sectionwise image of each categorical kernel inclusion as the kernel of its component. The component of the restriction unit is restriction from U to U intersect V, by restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app and the image/preimage formula for an open inclusion. After pushforward, sections and the inclusion are those over f inverse U. Thus both sectionwise ranges consist of sections of F(f inverse U) restricting to zero on f inverse (U intersect Z complement). Equality of their underlying sets gives equality of the actual linear submodules, with their given scalar actions.

source.place: Tag 07ZQ, lemma-push-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, final sentence of proof hint: match the sheaves directly

proof.text: Let $\beta:\mathcal H\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*\mathcal F$ be the given module-sheaf isomorphism. For any open $U\subseteq Y$ and $h\in\mathcal H(U)$, naturality gives $\beta_U(h)|_{U\setminus Z}=\beta_{U\setminus Z}(h|_{U\setminus Z})$. Since $\beta_{U\setminus Z}$ is an injective linear isomorphism, the left side vanishes if and only if $h|_{U\setminus Z}=0$. Thus the componentwise linear bijections $\beta_U$ and their inverses restrict to bijections between the supported submodule of $\mathcal H(U)$ and $\mathcal K_Y(U)$. Their naturality is inherited from $\beta$ and $\beta^{-1}$. Step 3 identifies this latter subsheaf with $f_*\mathcal K_X$, proving the final assertion.

source.place: Tag 07ZQ, lemma-push-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, equality of supported submodules; elementary naturality consequence for an isomorphism
